draft.title: Volume and capacity units
card: Volume is the space a solid takes up, in cubic units such as \(\text{cm}^{3}\) and \(\text{m}^{3}\). Capacity is how much a container holds, in units such as mL and L.
Cubic units change by more than length units do. Since \(1\) m \(= 100\) cm, we get \(1 \text{ m}^{3} = 100 \times 100 \times 100 = 1{,}000{,}000 \text{ cm}^{3}\).
A tank holds 3 L. Since \(1\) L \(= 1000\) mL, it holds \(3 \times 1000 = 3000\) mL, which is \(3000 \text{ cm}^{3}\).
draft.remember: \(1 \text{ cm}^{3} = 1\) mL and \(1 \text{ m}^{3} = 1000\) L. A cubic unit changes by the length factor cubed.

a.q: A fish tank holds 12 L of water. What is this in \(\text{cm}^{3}\)?
a.why: \(1\) L \(= 1000\) mL and \(1\) mL \(= 1 \text{ cm}^{3}\), so \(12\) L \(= 12 \times 1000 = 12{,}000 \text{ cm}^{3}\). Multiplying by only 100 would give 1200, which treats the litre like a length conversion.

b.q: A swimming pool has a volume of \(45 \text{ m}^{3}\). How many litres of water does it hold when full?
b.why: \(1 \text{ m}^{3} = 1000\) L, so \(45 \text{ m}^{3} = 45 \times 1000 = 45{,}000\) L. The option 45,000,000 comes from using \(1{,}000{,}000\) cm³ per m³, which gives cm³ and not litres.

proposal.title: Volume and capacity units
card: Volume is the space a solid takes up, in cubic units such as \(\text{cm}^{3}\) and \(\text{m}^{3}\). Capacity is how much a container holds, in units such as mL and L.
Cubic units change by more than length units do. Since \(1\) m \(= 100\) cm, \(1 \text{ m}^{3}\) is \(100 \times 100 \times 100\), which is \(1{,}000{,}000 \text{ cm}^{3}\).
For example, a jug holds 3 L. Since \(1\) L \(= 1000\) mL, it holds \(3 \times 1000 = 3000\) mL, which is \(3000 \text{ cm}^{3}\).
proposal.remember: Litres link to cubic units through mL and \(\text{m}^{3}\). A cubic unit changes by the length factor cubed.

b.q: A swimming pool has a volume of \(45 \text{ m}^{3}\). How many litres of water does it hold when full?
